cards.title: input() gives text
cards.body: `input()` always gives back text, even when the user types digits. Adding two pieces of text glues them together.
cards.code:
a = input()
b = input()
print(a + b)

cards.title: int() makes a number
cards.body: Wrap `input()` in `int()` to turn the text into a whole number. Now the maths works.
cards.code:
a = int(input())
b = int(input())
print(a - b)

cards.title: print() shows numbers too
cards.body: `print()` works with numbers and with whole calculations.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: Both values are strings in quotes, so + joins them into 44.
